name: Title Tracks
label: Dischord
lede: Q and Not U's drummer stepped out from behind the kit, picked up a guitar, and spent a decade writing tight, bright, record-collector power pop, some of it mixed in glorious mono.

eras.title: Out from behind the drums
eras.text: John Davis had spent seven years as the drummer in Q and Not U, one of Dischord's sharpest bands of the 2000s. When Q and Not U ended in 2005 he went looking for something poppier, first in the duo Georgie James and then on his own as Title Tracks, singing and playing guitar.

years.h: Q and Not U break up
years.p: John Davis's band Q and Not U disbands after finishing its tour commitments and a short farewell stand at the Black Cat in Washington.

years.h: John Davis and Laura Burhenn form Georgie James
years.p: John Davis teams up with singer and pianist [[Laura Burhenn|50174deb-4b25-41f5-9205-ae7b8b2f2118]]; the two bond over pop records from the 1950s to the '70s. As [[Georgie James|c4cfd21d-fd5e-45ae-88f2-413f9e15d944]] they sign to Saddle Creek and release Places in September 2007.

years.h: Georgie James break up; John Davis starts Title Tracks
years.p: John Davis had been writing solo songs since early 2008 while still in Georgie James. When the duo split that August, he founded Title Tracks; Laura Burhenn went on to [[The Mynabirds|daa0c966-31a1-4754-b293-67ffe5b4ac18]].
years.xp: Georgie James had signed to Saddle Creek in spring 2007 after a first single on Burhenn's own Laboratory Records, and Places followed that September. The breakup was announced on August 4, 2008, with both saying they hoped to focus on solo projects.

eras.title: A record collector's pop band
eras.text: Dischord put out Title Tracks' first single, then the band moved its albums to Ernest Jenning Record Co. Dischord's bio credits John Davis with an almost scientific approach to songwriting, built on years of crate-digging, radio DJ shifts and touring the world.

years.cap: Every Little Bit Hurts / Found Out, Dischord No. 163
years.h: Title Tracks' Every Little Bit Hurts · Dischord No. 163
years.p: A seven-inch for seven dollars: Every Little Bit Hurts backed with Found Out, recorded with [[Chad Clark|f3f09e99-e31c-4aa2-99e4-0b4e59e72f87]] of [[Beauty Pill|976b28a1-dd68-4c43-ba08-ba15b58963b2]]. Live, John Davis is joined by [[Michael Cotterman|c675284d-bfe6-4df0-89fc-0aca7a5372d5]] (bass), Andrew Black (drums) and Meredith Munoz (keys, guitar, vocals).
years.xp: Every Little Bit Hurts was recorded at Silver Sonya. It's the only Title Tracks record on Dischord. The label kept carrying the band's later records in its store, and Dischord's own pages still list all four.

years.h: Title Tracks' debut album It Was Easy on Ernest Jenning
years.p: John Davis plays most of the instruments himself and re-records both songs from the Dischord single. Guests include saxophonist Kriston Capps and [[Camera Obscura|94219793-a46b-4c39-9397-e05ad633f32d]] singer [[Tracyanne Campbell|4b10d405-48cb-4bf3-b7d0-98b509428f41]].
years.xp:
Dischord's store copy for It Was Easy calls Title Tracks the solo band of John Davis, formerly of Q and Not U, and flags that Every Little Bit Hurts and Found Out appear here in different versions.

The live band that toured it from February through May was Michael Cotterman, Andrew Black and Meredith Munoz.

years.h: Title Tracks tour North America for four months
years.p: Title Tracks tour North America from February through May 2010 behind It Was Easy.

years.h: In Blank, Title Tracks' second album, mixed in mono
years.p: Ten John Davis originals plus a cover of The Flamin' Groovies' I Can't Hide, released by Ernest Jenning and Windian and, in Dischord's words, mixed in glorious mono.

eras.title: One more long dream
eras.text: Five years after In Blank, Title Tracks came back as a trio for Long Dream. It turned out to be the last record: the band has been inactive since 2017.

years.p: Title Tracks' third album, on Ernest Jenning, made by a three-piece: John Davis, Michael Cotterman, and Elmer Sharp on drums. Sharp was the last in a line of drummers that also included [[Mike Sneeringer|50bd1658-4cfa-4e9c-8c33-778d4b6452d6]].
Title Tracks stop releasing records and playing after Long Dream. Dischord lists the band's active years as 2008–2017.
